original_test_intent: Demonstrate that an injected uncorrectable memory error on the intended GNR DRAM row triggers the expected reset and boot-time Soft PPR flow, with firmware qualifying and repairing the row and reporting passed PprRepairStatus.
original_method: Record platform/DIMM topology, harness and settings baseline; apply/verify the complete source enablement plus Soft PPR, Force-PPR-UCE, fast-boot and serial knobs; prove what harness address0x0 targets; preserve logs and establish continuous serial/OOB capture; halt/reset injector, issue one exact UCE and `go()`; attribute the automatic reset to that UCE, retain serial across boot, identify the same bad row, DDR PPR request, fast-boot state, repair action and passed status; verify DIMM/OS/BMC health and restore temporary settings without reinjection.
manual_activity: Intel-qualified owner/FAE validates target and harness, controls injection and recovery, and observes continuous serial through the expected automatic reset; agent may correlate retained evidence.
required_inputs: GNR stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS and exact DIMM/DRAM-row topology
CScripts harness version/hash/license and address0x0 UCE target semantics
Project mapping/restoration for all source BIOS/GRUB/DFX/ELog/WHEA/PPR/fast-boot/serial knobs
Expected UCE MCA/reset signature and maximum reset/POST/boot time
Serial fields identifying bad row, DDR PPR request, fast-boot disable, action and PprRepairStatus
Dedicated window, data/workload isolation and independent OOB/BIOS recovery
safety_requirements: Use only a dedicated workload-free SUT and approved sacrificial row
Do not inject at 0x0 until the vendor harness proves its physical target and non-OS semantics
Preserve all logs/settings and arm serial/OOB capture before halt/injection
Issue exactly one UCE; stop on wrong target/severity, missing reset, reset loop, POST failure or failed/absent PPR status
Do not reset or reinject automatically when the expected reset fails
Restore all debug/security/PPR settings only after evidence capture and verify final DIMM/OS/BMC health
agent_execution_scope: Observe one approved UCE/go sequence and retain continuous reset/boot/PPR evidence
Correlate the same row and final health/restoration
Do not select target, change settings, inject/reset/retry independently or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve address0x0 target and UCE/reset semantics
Approve BIOS/PPR/fast-boot configuration and expected serial fields
Approve crash/reboot timeout and OOB recovery
Review same-row repair/status and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Coverage mismatch: generic dmesg/SEL tails are supporting only and cannot establish the source automatic reset, bad-row qualification, DDR PPR request/action or passed status.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the exact approved console flow `halt(); resetInjectorLockCheck(); injectMemError(0x0, errType="uce"); go()` with continuous serial/OOB capture through its expected automatic reset.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Complete BIOS matrix, Soft PPR, Force-PPR-UCE, fast boot/cold boot, RAS/serial levels, address0x0 UCE, automatic reset, PPR serial/status, Common branch and 30/30-minute estimate are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one topology-bound UCE and prove continuous same-row boot-time repair across the expected automatic reset.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds immutable row identity, reset attribution/timing, continuous evidence and audited restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A reboot plus UCE log does not prove firmware qualified or repaired the intended row, or that PprRepairStatus passed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A UCE can reset-loop or prevent boot; Force PPR may modify DRAM repair state and a wrong target can damage the wrong row.

project_override_considerations: Fast-boot transitions and Force-PPR scope are firmware-specific and require explicit expected before/after state; no CE or row160 procedure may substitute for this UCE path.
expected_evidence: Platform/DIMM/row identity, harness and before/after settings matrix
Address0x0 target proof and one exact UCE injector transcript
Expected UCE MCA/reset cause plus reset/POST/boot timeline
Continuous serial bad-row qualification and DDR PPR request with fast-boot state
Same-row PPR action and passed PprRepairStatus
Supporting ELog/OS/SEL, final health/restoration and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The UCE injection, expected reset, post-reboot PPR request/action and passed-status criterion form one coherent boot-time repair flow.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is explicit; harness, target mapping, firmware settings and recovery are identifiable RPUC prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row161 Wistron-System RAS-00118-V002: approve GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS, CScripts version/hash/license, address0x0-to-socket/IMC/channel/DIMM/DRAM-row mapping and expected UCE MCA/reset signature; map/restore every source BIOS/GRUB/DFX/Soft-PPR/Force-PPR/fast-boot/serial knob; define reset/POST/boot timeouts, continuous serial bad-row/DDR-PPR/fast-boot/action/PprRepairStatus fields, same-row correlation and OOB recovery with no automatic reset or reinjection.

review_improvement: Restores the source's automatic-reset and firmware repair acceptance, replacing generic log tails with target-bound continuous serial evidence and no-retry recovery control.
independent_technical_reasoning: The UCE is expected to remove normal OS continuity, so post-return dmesg cannot prove the firmware path. The decisive chain starts with a known physical row, attributes the reset to one UCE, and follows that row through qualification, persistent PPR request, repair action and passed status. Address0x0 is a harness coordinate whose meaning cannot be inferred. Any extra reset or reinjection destroys attribution and can create a reset loop, so recovery remains operator-owned.
